authored_against: High School Earth, Space, and Environmental Science, Grade 12. Keys state established science at this course level; they are not extracted from the source, which states a focus and generic objectives.

relationships: A system is defined by its boundary, its components, and the flows of matter and energy across that boundary.
System behaviour arises from the interactions between components, so it cannot be predicted from any component alone.
Where the boundary is drawn determines what counts as internal behaviour and what counts as an input or output.
accepted_alternative_framings: Box-and-arrow diagrams, stock-and-flow diagrams, and written system descriptions are all acceptable model forms.
disqualifying_errors: Describing a system with no boundary stated.
Explaining a whole-system behaviour from one component in isolation.
Claiming a system model captures the real system completely.
topics.out_of_scope: Formal systems dynamics mathematics is beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Earth and space processes span timescales from seconds to billions of years and spatial scales from grains to galaxies.
relationships: A process observable at one scale may be invisible at another, so the scale of observation determines what can be concluded.
Slow processes accumulate large effects over long times, which is why geologic change is substantial despite being imperceptible year to year.
Extrapolating a rate measured over a short interval to a much longer one requires evidence that the rate is constant.
disqualifying_errors: Extrapolating a short-term rate across geologic time with no evidence that the rate is constant.
Concluding a process does not occur because it is not observable within a human lifetime.
Comparing measurements made at different spatial scales as though they were equivalent.
topics.out_of_scope: Formal scaling theory and fractal analysis are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: A proxy is a measurable quantity that stands in for a quantity that cannot be measured directly, and it requires a calibrated relationship between the two.
relationships: Ice cores, tree rings, sediment layers, corals, and isotope ratios are proxies for past conditions.
A proxy carries the uncertainty of the calibration as well as of the measurement itself.
Independent proxies agreeing is what makes a reconstruction robust; a single proxy carries much weaker support.
disqualifying_errors: Treating a proxy measurement as a direct measurement of the quantity it stands for.
Reporting a proxy reconstruction with no reference to its calibration or uncertainty.
Basing a reconstruction on one proxy and presenting it as settled.
topics.out_of_scope: Specific proxy calibration methodology and age-model construction are beyond this course.

relationships: Geoscience data carries uncertainty from measurement, from sampling in space and time, and from the models used to interpret it.
Uncertainty is a quantified statement about how well something is known; it is not an admission that nothing is known.
A conclusion is stated with the uncertainty attached, so that a reader can judge what it supports.
accepted_alternative_framings: Ranges, error bars, and stated confidence language are all acceptable ways to express uncertainty at this level.
disqualifying_errors: Treating a stated uncertainty as grounds for dismissing a well-supported conclusion.
Reporting a geoscience result with no indication of uncertainty or sampling limits.
Claiming two values differ when the difference is within the stated uncertainty.
topics.out_of_scope: Formal statistical inference and Bayesian methods are beyond this course.

relationships: Axis range, scale type, and baseline choice change how a graph reads without changing the underlying data.
A graph states its data source, its date, and its units, or the reader cannot check it.
Extrapolation beyond the data is labelled as such, because the data does not support it.
accepted_alternative_framings: Linear and logarithmic scales are both legitimate; the choice is disclosed and justified by what needs to be shown.
disqualifying_errors: Presenting an extrapolation as though it were measured data.
Choosing an axis range or baseline that conceals or exaggerates the effect being discussed, without disclosure.
Drawing a conclusion from a graph with no source, units, or date given.
topics.out_of_scope: Formal data visualisation theory is beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Correlation between two variables does not establish that one causes the other.
relationships: Two variables can correlate because one causes the other, because a third factor drives both, or by coincidence in a limited sample.
Establishing causation requires a mechanism, evidence that cause precedes effect, and where possible a controlled comparison.
In Earth science, controlled experiments are often impossible, so causal claims rest on mechanism plus multiple independent lines of evidence.
disqualifying_errors: Inferring causation from correlation alone.
Rejecting a well-supported causal claim on the grounds that the evidence is correlational, when mechanism and multiple lines of evidence are present.
Asserting a mechanism with no evidence and treating that as having established causation.
topics.out_of_scope: Formal causal inference frameworks are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Stars release energy by fusing lighter nuclei into heavier ones, principally hydrogen into helium during the main sequence.
relationships: Fusion requires the extreme temperature and pressure found in stellar cores, because positively charged nuclei repel one another.
The energy released corresponds to the small mass difference between the reactants and the products.
The outward pressure from fusion balances the inward pull of gravity, which is what keeps a main-sequence star stable.
accepted_alternative_framings: Naming the proton-proton chain or the CNO cycle is correct but not required.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming stars are powered by chemical combustion.
Claiming stellar energy comes from fission of heavy nuclei.
Claiming fusion occurs throughout a star rather than in its core region.
topics.out_of_scope: Reaction rate calculations and stellar structure equations are beyond this course.

topics.focus: the sun's energy budget and lifespan
fixed_facts: The Sun is roughly 4.6 billion years old and is about halfway through its main-sequence lifetime.
The Sun will end as a white dwarf, not as a supernova.
relationships: The Sun's energy output is set by the rate of fusion in its core, which is regulated by the balance between gravity and pressure.
Essentially all the energy driving Earth's surface processes, weather, and life originates from the Sun, with geothermal and tidal energy as small additional contributions.
A star's lifetime depends on its mass: more massive stars burn far more quickly and live far shorter lives.
accepted_alternative_framings: Approximate ages and lifetimes such as 'about four and a half billion years' are correct; exact figures are not required.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming the Sun will explode as a supernova.
Claiming more massive stars live longer because they have more fuel.
Claiming the Sun's energy comes from a source other than nuclear fusion.
topics.out_of_scope: Solar interior modelling and helioseismology are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: A star's mass determines its life cycle and its end state: white dwarf for low and intermediate masses, neutron star or black hole for high masses.
relationships: Stars form from collapsing clouds of gas and dust, spend most of their lives fusing hydrogen on the main sequence, and then evolve as their core fuel is exhausted.
Low and intermediate mass stars expand to red giants, shed their outer layers, and leave a white dwarf.
High-mass stars end in supernova explosions, leaving a neutron star or a black hole.
accepted_alternative_framings: Hertzsprung-Russell diagram reasoning is correct but not required.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming all stars end their lives as supernovae.
Claiming a star's life cycle depends principally on its brightness rather than on its mass.
Claiming stars burn fuel chemically.
topics.out_of_scope: Detailed stellar evolution tracks and mass-loss modelling are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Hydrogen and helium formed in the early universe; elements up to iron are produced by fusion in stars; most elements heavier than iron are produced by neutron capture in evolved stars and in explosive events.
relationships: Fusion releases energy up to iron, and beyond iron fusion consumes rather than releases energy, which is why stellar fusion does not build the heaviest elements.
Heavier elements are dispersed into space by stellar winds and supernovae, enriching the material from which later stars and planets form.
The atoms in Earth and in living things were produced in earlier generations of stars.
accepted_alternative_framings: Naming the s-process and r-process, or describing neutron capture in general terms, are equally correct.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming all elements were produced in the Big Bang.
Claiming stellar core fusion produces elements heavier than iron by releasing energy.
Claiming heavy elements formed on Earth rather than being inherited from earlier stars.
topics.out_of_scope: Nuclear reaction network modelling and isotopic yield calculations are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Each element produces a characteristic pattern of spectral lines, which is how the composition of distant objects is determined.
relationships: Emission lines appear where atoms release specific energies; absorption lines appear where atoms remove those same energies from light passing through.
Because the line pattern is characteristic of the element, a spectrum identifies which elements are present without any sample being collected.
Line positions also carry information about motion, through Doppler shift, and about conditions such as temperature and pressure.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming spectral line patterns are the same for different elements.
Claiming composition of distant stars is determined by collecting material from them.
Confusing an absorption spectrum with an emission spectrum in interpreting which material lies where.
topics.out_of_scope: Quantitative abundance determination and line-profile analysis are beyond this course.

relationships: Communicating astronomical results means distinguishing what was measured, what was inferred from a model, and how confident the conclusion is.
Astronomical images are frequently processed and colour-mapped, and a communication says so rather than presenting them as direct views.
Scale statements need explicit units and comparisons, because astronomical magnitudes are outside everyday experience.
disqualifying_errors: Presenting a false-colour or composite astronomical image as a direct visual observation.
Reporting an inferred property, such as a star's mass, as though it had been measured directly.
Stating an astronomical distance or age with no units or uncertainty.
topics.out_of_scope: Science communication theory and image processing methods are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Redshift is a shift of spectral lines toward longer wavelengths; blueshift is a shift toward shorter wavelengths.
relationships: Redshift is identified by the whole characteristic line pattern of an element being displaced, which is what distinguishes it from an object simply being red.
Cosmological redshift arises because space itself has expanded while the light was in transit, stretching its wavelength.
Measuring the shift of known line patterns is how the recession of distant galaxies is determined.
accepted_alternative_framings: Describing cosmological redshift as expansion of space, and the Doppler analogy as an approximation for nearby objects, are both acceptable.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming a red-looking star is redshifted for that reason.
Claiming cosmological redshift means galaxies are moving through space away from a central point.
Claiming redshift shortens wavelengths.
topics.out_of_scope: Relativistic Doppler formulas and scale-factor cosmology are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Almost all distant galaxies show redshift, indicating that the universe is expanding.
relationships: Observers in any galaxy would see the same pattern of recession, because the expansion has no centre within the universe.
Nearby galaxies can show blueshift, because local gravitational motion can exceed the expansion at short distances.
The expansion carries galaxies apart; galaxies are not flying outward through pre-existing space from an explosion site.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming the universe has a centre from which galaxies are receding.
Claiming the Big Bang was an explosion at a point in existing space.
Claiming every galaxy without exception shows redshift.
topics.out_of_scope: Peculiar velocity corrections and large-scale structure dynamics are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: More distant galaxies recede faster, with recession speed approximately proportional to distance.
relationships: The proportionality between recession speed and distance is what is expected if space is expanding uniformly.
The relationship allows distance to be estimated from redshift, once the constant of proportionality is calibrated.
Extrapolating the expansion backward gives an estimate of the time since the expansion began.
accepted_alternative_framings: Naming the constant of proportionality the Hubble constant, or describing the relationship without the name, are equally correct.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming all galaxies recede at the same speed regardless of distance.
Claiming the relationship shows the Milky Way is at the centre of the expansion.
Treating the calibration constant as exactly known when its measured value carries real uncertainty.
topics.out_of_scope: Distance ladder methodology and tension between measured values of the constant are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: The cosmic microwave background is faint radiation reaching Earth from every direction, with a spectrum matching a body at about 2.7 kelvin.
relationships: The background radiation is light released when the early universe first became transparent, stretched to microwave wavelengths by the expansion since.
Its near-uniformity across the sky, with small measured variations, is a strong constraint on models of the early universe.
It was predicted before it was detected, which is why its discovery was decisive evidence.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming the background radiation comes from a particular direction or source in the sky.
Claiming the background is perfectly uniform with no variations; the small variations are themselves key evidence.
Claiming the background is light currently emitted by distant galaxies.
topics.out_of_scope: Power spectrum analysis and cosmological parameter fitting are beyond this course.

topics.focus: composition of matter in the universe
fixed_facts: Ordinary matter in the universe is overwhelmingly hydrogen and helium, in a ratio close to three to one by mass.
relationships: The observed hydrogen and helium proportions match what a hot early universe predicts, which is an independent line of evidence for the model.
All elements heavier than helium together make up only a small fraction of ordinary matter.
Ordinary matter itself accounts for a minority of the universe's total mass and energy content, with dark matter and dark energy making up the rest.
accepted_alternative_framings: Approximate proportions such as 'about three quarters hydrogen' are correct; exact figures are not required.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming heavy elements make up a large fraction of the universe's ordinary matter.
Claiming the elemental proportions were produced entirely in stars.
Claiming ordinary matter accounts for most of the universe's mass and energy.
topics.out_of_scope: Big Bang nucleosynthesis calculations and dark matter detection methods are beyond this course.

topics.focus: constructing an explanation from multiple evidence lines
relationships: The strength of the Big Bang model rests on several independent lines agreeing: galaxy redshifts, the microwave background, and the light-element abundances.
Independent lines of evidence converging carries far more weight than any single line, because they fail in different ways.
An explanation states which observations it accounts for and which it does not.
disqualifying_errors: Presenting one line of evidence as establishing the model on its own.
Omitting an observation the explanation does not account for.
Treating independent confirmations as though they were repetitions of the same measurement.
topics.out_of_scope: Formal model comparison and likelihood analysis are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Gravity provides the force that keeps a body in orbit, and an orbiting body is continuously accelerating toward the body it orbits.
relationships: An orbit is the result of a body's sideways motion combined with continuous gravitational acceleration toward the central body.
An orbiting object has weight; it appears weightless because it and everything with it are in free fall together.
The two bodies attract each other equally and both orbit their common centre of mass, which lies inside the more massive body when the mass difference is large.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming there is no gravity where satellites orbit.
Claiming an outward force balances gravity to hold an object in orbit.
Claiming an orbiting object is not accelerating because its speed is nearly constant.
topics.out_of_scope: Orbital perturbation theory and n-body dynamics are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Planetary orbits are ellipses with the Sun at one focus.
The square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis.
relationships: A planet moves faster when nearer the Sun and slower when farther away, sweeping equal areas in equal times.
The period-radius relationship holds for any set of bodies orbiting the same central mass, which is why it applies to moons and satellites too.
Kepler's relationships describe the motion; Newton's law of gravitation explains why it takes that form.
accepted_alternative_framings: Naming the laws by number, or describing them, are equally correct.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming the Sun sits at the centre of a planet's elliptical orbit rather than at a focus.
Claiming orbital period is directly proportional to orbital radius.
Claiming a planet moves at constant speed throughout an elliptical orbit.
topics.out_of_scope: Derivation of Kepler's laws from Newtonian gravitation is acceptable but not required.

fixed_facts: A body in a larger orbit around the same central mass has a longer period and a lower orbital speed.
relationships: The period-radius relationship means a satellite raised to a higher orbit takes longer to complete each circuit.
Orbital speed decreases with increasing orbital radius, even though the total orbital energy increases.
Because the relationship depends on the central mass, measuring a satellite's period and orbital radius determines that mass.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming a satellite in a higher orbit moves faster because it has more energy.
Claiming orbital period depends on the mass of the orbiting body.
Claiming period is proportional to radius rather than following the square-cube relationship.
topics.out_of_scope: Orbital transfer manoeuvres and delta-v calculation are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: In an elliptical orbit, kinetic and gravitational potential energy exchange while the total remains constant in the absence of other forces.
relationships: A body speeds up as it approaches the central body, converting potential energy into kinetic, and slows as it recedes.
Total orbital energy is conserved for an isolated two-body system, so an orbit does not decay without an external influence such as atmospheric drag.
Most planetary orbits in the solar system are close to circular; textbook diagrams exaggerate their ellipticity.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming Earth's orbit is strongly elliptical, and using that to explain the seasons.
Claiming an orbiting body loses energy continuously in the absence of drag or another external force.
Claiming kinetic energy is greatest at the point farthest from the central body.
topics.out_of_scope: Vis-viva equation and orbital element formalism are beyond this course.

relationships: An orbital simulation advances position and velocity in steps using the gravitational force, and its accuracy depends on the step size and method.
Simulation output is a prediction conditional on the initial conditions and assumptions supplied, and both are stated.
A simulation that does not conserve energy over long runs is exhibiting numerical error, not physics.
disqualifying_errors: Presenting simulation output as observational data.
Attributing a simulated orbit's drift to a physical effect without checking the numerical method.
Reporting simulation results without stating initial conditions or assumptions.
topics.out_of_scope: Numerical integrator theory and error analysis are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: The inner planets are small and rocky; the outer planets are large and gas- or ice-rich, and this pattern reflects conditions in the forming solar nebula.
relationships: The solar system formed from a rotating disc of gas and dust, which is why the planets orbit in nearly the same plane and direction.
Temperature in the disc decreased with distance from the young Sun, so volatile materials could condense only in the outer regions.
Asteroids, comets, and Kuiper belt objects are remnants of that formation process and carry evidence about it.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming the planets formed independently and were later captured by the Sun.
Claiming the inner-outer composition difference is a coincidence rather than a consequence of formation conditions.
Claiming the asteroid belt is the remains of a destroyed planet.
topics.out_of_scope: Planetary migration models and exoplanet system comparison are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Plate motion is directly measured today by satellite geodesy, at rates of centimetres per year.
relationships: Evidence includes matching coastlines and rock sequences across oceans, matching fossil distributions, seafloor age patterns, earthquake and volcano distributions, and direct measurement.
The distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes in narrow bands marks plate boundaries.
No single line of evidence established plate tectonics; the convergence of many did.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming continents plough through oceanic crust rather than moving as parts of plates.
Claiming plate motion is too slow to be measured directly.
Claiming earthquakes and volcanoes are distributed randomly across Earth's surface.
topics.out_of_scope: Quantitative plate kinematics and GPS processing methods are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Oceanic crust is youngest at mid-ocean ridges and progressively older away from them, symmetrically on both sides.
The oceanic crust is far younger than the continental crust, because it is continually created and destroyed.
relationships: New oceanic crust forms at ridges and records the direction of Earth's magnetic field as it cools.
Because Earth's magnetic field has reversed many times, the seafloor carries symmetric bands of alternating magnetisation on either side of a ridge.
The symmetry of the pattern is direct evidence of seafloor spreading.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming the seafloor is oldest at the ridges.
Claiming the magnetic stripes record variations in rock type rather than reversals of Earth's field.
Claiming oceanic and continental crust are of comparable age.
topics.out_of_scope: Magnetostratigraphic dating methodology and geodynamo theory are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Earth's mantle is solid rock that deforms and flows very slowly; it is not a liquid layer.
relationships: Heat from Earth's interior, from residual formation heat and radioactive decay, drives slow convective flow in the mantle.
Mantle flow, together with the pull of dense subducting slabs and the push at ridges, drives plate motion.
The mantle behaves as a solid on short timescales and flows on geological ones, which is why seismic shear waves pass through it.
accepted_alternative_framings: Attributing plate motion to mantle convection, or to a combination including slab pull and ridge push, are both acceptable at this level.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming the plates float on a layer of liquid magma.
Claiming Earth's internal heat comes principally from the Sun.
Claiming the entire outer core and mantle are molten; only the outer core is liquid.
topics.out_of_scope: Mantle rheology and geodynamic modelling are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Oceanic crust is denser and thinner than continental crust, which is why oceanic crust subducts beneath continental crust.
relationships: Oceanic crust forms at spreading ridges from mantle-derived magma and is returned to the mantle at subduction zones.
Continental crust is less dense, so it resists subduction and can survive for billions of years.
Subduction generates magma that rises to build volcanic arcs and adds to continental crust over time.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming continental crust subducts beneath oceanic crust.
Claiming oceanic and continental crust have the same composition and density.
Claiming continental crust is continuously recycled at the same rate as oceanic crust.
topics.out_of_scope: Igneous petrogenesis and crustal growth modelling are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Earth is about 4.5 billion years old, determined principally from radiometric dating of meteorites and the oldest terrestrial minerals.
The half-life of a radioactive isotope is unaffected by temperature, pressure, or chemical combination.
relationships: Radiometric dating measures the ratio of a parent isotope to its decay product and converts it to elapsed time using the known half-life.
The method requires a closed system since formation, which is why samples are tested for disturbance and why multiple isotope systems are cross-checked.
Different isotope pairs suit different age ranges, and agreement between independent systems is what makes an age robust.
accepted_alternative_framings: Approximate statements such as 'about four and a half billion years' are correct; the precise figure is not required.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming decay rates vary with environmental conditions in a way that undermines dating.
Claiming radiometric dating gives an age for a rock without any assumption about the system being closed.
Claiming carbon dating is used to date rocks billions of years old.
topics.out_of_scope: Isochron construction and closure temperature theory are beyond this course.

relationships: A geologic history is reconstructed by combining relative dating of structures with absolute ages and with evidence about depositional environment.
Cross-cutting relationships, inclusions, and unconformities each constrain the sequence of events.
A reconstruction states which parts are well constrained and which rest on fewer lines of evidence.
accepted_alternative_framings: Naming the stratigraphic principles, or applying them without the names, are equally correct.
disqualifying_errors: Applying superposition to a sequence with evidence of overturning without accounting for it.
Treating an unconformity as evidence that no time passed rather than that record is missing.
Presenting a reconstruction as settled where only one line of evidence supports it.
topics.out_of_scope: Basin analysis and quantitative subsidence modelling are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Weathering breaks rock down in place; erosion transports the products; deposition lays them down elsewhere.
relationships: Physical weathering fragments rock without changing its composition; chemical weathering alters the minerals themselves.
Rates depend on climate, rock type, slope, and vegetation cover, so they vary greatly between settings.
Chemical weathering of silicate rock consumes atmospheric carbon dioxide, linking surface processes to the long-term carbon cycle.
accepted_alternative_framings: Physical and mechanical weathering are the same category.
disqualifying_errors: Using weathering and erosion interchangeably.
Claiming chemical weathering rates are independent of climate.
Claiming weathering rates are uniform across all rock types and settings.
topics.out_of_scope: Quantitative weathering flux calculation is beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Water expands on freezing, so ice is less dense than liquid water and floats.
Water has an unusually high specific heat capacity and a high heat of vaporisation.
relationships: Water's polarity and its hydrogen bonding account for its high specific heat, high heat of vaporisation, high surface tension, and its capacity to dissolve many substances.
Ice floating means lakes freeze from the top down, insulating the water beneath and allowing aquatic life to survive winter.
Water's high specific heat moderates the climate near large water bodies and makes the ocean a large thermal reservoir.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming ice is denser than liquid water.
Claiming water's anomalous properties arise from something other than its polarity and hydrogen bonding.
Claiming water dissolves all substances equally well.
topics.out_of_scope: Quantitative thermodynamic properties and solvation modelling are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Groundwater occupies pore spaces and fractures in rock and sediment; it does not generally flow in open underground rivers.
relationships: Surface water and groundwater are connected: streams gain from or lose to groundwater depending on the water table.
Groundwater moves far more slowly than surface water, so contamination is slow to appear and slow to clear.
Extraction faster than recharge lowers the water table and can cause land subsidence and saltwater intrusion.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming groundwater flows in underground rivers throughout the subsurface.
Claiming surface water and groundwater are independent supplies.
Claiming an aquifer refills as quickly as it is pumped.
topics.out_of_scope: Darcy's law calculation and aquifer modelling are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: A positive feedback amplifies an initial change; a negative feedback damps it.
relationships: Ice-albedo feedback is positive: warming melts reflective ice, exposing darker surfaces that absorb more energy and warm further.
Silicate weathering is a negative feedback on long timescales: warming speeds weathering, which removes carbon dioxide and cools.
Feedbacks determine whether a perturbation is amplified or damped, and identifying their sign is central to predicting system behaviour.
disqualifying_errors: Equating positive feedback with a beneficial outcome and negative feedback with a harmful one.
Describing an amplifying process as a negative feedback.
Claiming Earth systems contain only stabilising feedbacks.
topics.out_of_scope: Quantitative feedback strength and climate sensitivity calculation are beyond this course.

relationships: Land clearing, agriculture, construction, damming, and channel modification change rates of erosion, deposition, infiltration, and runoff.
Altering one part of a surface system changes others, often downstream or after a delay.
Human activity now moves more sediment and earth material annually than many natural processes do.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming a local land-use change has only local effects.
Claiming human effects on surface processes are negligible compared with natural ones.
Claiming an engineered channel or dam removes flood risk rather than altering it.
topics.out_of_scope: Sediment budget quantification and hydrological modelling are beyond this course.

relationships: An investigation of water or earth materials states its sampling location, time, method, and the property measured, since all four affect the result.
Natural variability means a single sample characterises that sample, not the system it came from.
Measurements are compared against published values only where the method and conditions are comparable.
disqualifying_errors: Characterising a water body or a formation from a single sample.
Comparing a measurement against a published value obtained by a different method without saying so.
Reporting a field measurement without location, time, and method.
topics.out_of_scope: Analytical laboratory methods and quality assurance protocols are beyond this course.

topics.focus: energy flow into and out of Earth systems
fixed_facts: Earth's climate is set by the balance between incoming solar radiation and outgoing infrared radiation.
relationships: Incoming solar energy is absorbed, reflected, or scattered, and the reflective fraction is the albedo.
Earth radiates energy back to space as infrared, and long-term temperature is set by the balance between incoming and outgoing.
Anything that changes absorbed solar energy or outgoing infrared changes the balance and therefore the temperature.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming Earth's surface temperature is set by incoming solar radiation alone with no role for outgoing radiation.
Claiming Earth's internal heat is a major contributor to surface temperature.
Claiming a change in albedo has no effect on the energy balance.
topics.out_of_scope: Radiative transfer calculation and quantitative energy budget partitioning are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Greenhouse gases are largely transparent to incoming sunlight and absorb outgoing infrared radiation, re-emitting some of it back toward the surface.
The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth's surface far warmer than it would otherwise be and is necessary for life as it exists.
relationships: Water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide absorb infrared radiation because of how their molecules vibrate.
Adding greenhouse gases reduces outgoing infrared for a given surface temperature, so the surface warms until balance is restored.
The concern is the enhancement of the natural effect by gases added through human activity, not the existence of the effect.
accepted_alternative_framings: Describing the mechanism as absorption and re-emission of infrared, or as reduced outgoing longwave radiation, are both correct.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming greenhouse gases work by trapping heat like the glass of a greenhouse, which warms mainly by suppressing convection.
Claiming greenhouse gases block incoming sunlight.
Confusing the natural greenhouse effect with the enhanced effect from added gases, or treating the natural effect as the problem.
topics.out_of_scope: Radiative forcing calculation and line-by-line absorption modelling are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Burning fossil fuels transfers carbon from a long-term geological reservoir into the atmosphere far faster than natural processes return it.
relationships: Carbon moves between atmosphere, ocean, land biosphere, soils, and rock, on timescales ranging from years to millions of years.
The ocean has absorbed a large fraction of the carbon dioxide added by human activity, which has also made surface waters more acidic.
A carbon budget accounts for all sources and sinks; the atmospheric increase is the difference between what is added and what is taken up.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming carbon added to the atmosphere is removed on a timescale of a few years.
Claiming the fast biological cycle and the slow geological cycle operate at comparable rates.
Claiming ocean uptake of carbon dioxide has no chemical consequences for seawater.
topics.out_of_scope: Quantitative reservoir and flux figures, and carbonate chemistry calculations, are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Weather is the atmospheric state over hours to days; climate is the statistical description of weather over decades.
relationships: Climate is described by averages, ranges, and the frequency of extremes, over periods conventionally of thirty years or more.
An individual weather event neither confirms nor refutes a claim about climate, though a change in the frequency of such events is climate evidence.
Climate predictability and weather predictability are different problems: the long-term statistics can be projected even where individual days cannot.
disqualifying_errors: Using an individual cold or hot event as evidence for or against long-term climate change.
Claiming that because weather cannot be forecast beyond about two weeks, climate cannot be projected at all.
Treating climate and weather as the same quantity measured over different periods with no other distinction.
topics.out_of_scope: Attribution science methodology and extreme-value statistics are beyond this course.

relationships: Climate models are built from physical laws and are tested against past and present observations before being used for projection.
Projections are given as ranges under stated scenarios, because future emissions are a choice and the physics carries its own uncertainty.
Model uncertainty is quantified; it is not a statement that the projections carry no information.
accepted_alternative_framings: Describing projections by scenario, by range, or by ensemble spread are all acceptable.
disqualifying_errors: Treating a projection range as evidence that models are uninformative.
Presenting a single model run as a prediction rather than as one member of a range.
Claiming a scenario-based projection failed because emissions followed a different scenario.
topics.out_of_scope: Model intercomparison methodology and parameterisation schemes are beyond this course.

relationships: A forecast states what is projected, under what assumptions, over what period, and with what uncertainty.
A forecast is evaluated over many predictions against what actually occurred, not by a single instance.
Distinguishing a projection conditional on a scenario from an unconditional prediction is essential to evaluating either.
disqualifying_errors: Judging a probabilistic forecast wrong on the basis of one outcome.
Presenting a scenario-conditional projection as an unconditional prediction.
Reporting a forecast with no stated period, assumptions, or uncertainty.
topics.out_of_scope: Forecast verification statistics and skill scores are beyond this course.

topics.focus: the Great Oxidation Event and atmospheric change
fixed_facts: Earth's early atmosphere contained essentially no free oxygen; atmospheric oxygen accumulated from about 2.4 billion years ago, produced by photosynthesising organisms.
relationships: Oxygen-producing photosynthesis by cyanobacteria released oxygen that was first consumed by dissolved iron and other reduced material before accumulating in the atmosphere.
Banded iron formations in the rock record are evidence of that early oxygen being taken up by dissolved iron.
The rise of oxygen transformed surface chemistry and made aerobic metabolism, and eventually complex life, possible.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming Earth's atmosphere has always contained free oxygen at roughly present levels.
Claiming atmospheric oxygen was produced by geological outgassing rather than by photosynthesis.
Claiming oxygen accumulated immediately once photosynthesis began.
topics.out_of_scope: Isotopic evidence methodology and detailed Precambrian chronology are beyond this course.

topics.focus: coevolution of the geosphere and biosphere
relationships: Life has altered Earth's atmosphere, oceans, soils, and rocks, and those changes have in turn shaped the evolution of life.
Many rock types, including limestone, coal, and banded iron formations, exist because of biological activity.
The influence runs in both directions, which is why the systems are described as coevolving rather than one acting on the other.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming life adapted to Earth's conditions without altering them.
Claiming Earth's physical systems developed independently of the biosphere.
Claiming biologically produced rocks are chemically indistinguishable in origin from purely inorganic ones.
topics.out_of_scope: Earth system modelling of coevolution is beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Mineral, energy, water, and soil resources are distributed unevenly because of the specific geological and biological processes that concentrated them.
relationships: Ore deposits form where particular processes concentrated an element far above its average crustal abundance.
Fossil fuels formed where organic material accumulated, was buried, and was heated within a particular range of conditions.
A resource is economically usable only where concentration, accessibility, and extraction cost permit, so the physical presence of an element is not sufficient.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming resource distribution is random or a matter of chance.
Claiming an element's presence in the crust makes it available as a resource.
Claiming resource distribution follows political boundaries.
topics.out_of_scope: Ore genesis models and reserve estimation methodology are beyond this course.

fixed_facts: Earthquakes and volcanoes occur predominantly at plate boundaries, and their global distribution follows those boundaries.
relationships: Each hazard has a physical cause, and understanding the cause is what makes the hazard mappable and, in some cases, forecastable.
Hazard forecasting is generally probabilistic: the likelihood over a period can be estimated where the timing of a specific event cannot.
A hazard becomes a disaster through exposure and vulnerability, so risk depends on people and infrastructure as well as on the physical event.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming individual earthquakes can be predicted for a specific day and place with current science.
Claiming hazards occur at random with no relation to physical processes.
Treating hazard and risk as the same quantity.
topics.out_of_scope: Probabilistic seismic hazard analysis and eruption forecasting methods are beyond this course.

relationships: Where people settle has been shaped by access to water, arable soil, energy, materials, and transport routes.
Settlement in hazard-prone locations often reflects the resources that make those locations valuable, such as fertile volcanic soils and river floodplains.
Resource availability changes over time through depletion, technology, and climate, and settlement patterns respond with a lag.
disqualifying_errors: Claiming settlement patterns are unrelated to the physical distribution of resources.
Claiming people settle in hazardous places only through ignorance of the hazard.
Claiming resource availability at a location is fixed over time.
topics.out_of_scope: Human geography theory and economic modelling are beyond this course.

topics.focus: constructing arguments from geologic and biological evidence
relationships: An argument about Earth history links a claim to specific geologic and biological evidence through explicit reasoning about process.
Because controlled experiments on Earth history are impossible, arguments rest on multiple independent lines of evidence converging.
An argument states which parts of the claim the evidence establishes and which remain open.
disqualifying_errors: Presenting a single line of evidence as establishing a claim about Earth history.
Omitting evidence that does not fit the proposed reconstruction.
Treating the impossibility of controlled experiment as grounds for treating any reconstruction as equally supported.
topics.out_of_scope: Formal historical-science methodology is beyond this course.

relationships: Criteria state what a sustainability solution must achieve; constraints state its limits, including physical, economic, legal, and ethical ones.
Prioritising among criteria is a value judgement made explicit, not a measurement, and different stakeholders prioritise differently.
Physical constraints such as resource availability and energy balance cannot be traded away by preference.
disqualifying_errors: Presenting a prioritisation among criteria as though it were determined by the evidence alone.
Proposing a solution that violates a physical constraint such as conservation of energy or matter.
Declaring a solution best with no criteria stated.
topics.out_of_scope: Formal multi-criteria decision analysis is beyond this course.

topics.focus: cost-benefit analysis of energy and mineral resources
relationships: A full comparison of resource options accounts for the whole life cycle: extraction, processing, transport, use, and end of life.
Every energy and mineral option has environmental and social costs; the comparison is between different sets of costs, not between costly and costless options.
Costs and benefits fall on different groups and over different timescales, and a comparison that omits that is incomplete.
disqualifying_errors: Presenting any energy or mineral option as having no environmental cost.
Comparing options on operational effects alone while ignoring extraction, manufacture, or disposal.
Omitting who bears the costs and who receives the benefits.
topics.out_of_scope: Formal life-cycle assessment methodology and discounting are beyond this course.

relationships: A coupled-system simulation represents the interactions between components, and the coupling is often what produces the interesting behaviour.
Output depends on assumptions, parameters, and initial conditions, all of which are stated with the result.
A simulation is compared against observation where possible, and its limits are reported alongside its output.
disqualifying_errors: Presenting simulation output as observational data.
Reporting a simulation result without its assumptions or parameter choices.
Claiming a simulation is validated with no comparison against observation.
topics.out_of_scope: Numerical methods and formal model validation frameworks are beyond this course.

relationships: Refinement proceeds by testing against criteria, identifying a specific shortfall, and making a change aimed at it.
Changing one thing at a time keeps the effect of each change identifiable.
Unintended consequences are looked for deliberately, because a solution that shifts a problem elsewhere has not solved it.
disqualifying_errors: Changing several features at once and attributing the improvement to one.
Declaring a refinement successful without retesting against the criteria.
Reporting a solution as effective while omitting an effect it displaced elsewhere.
topics.out_of_scope: Formal design-of-experiments methodology is beyond this course.

relationships: Total resource demand depends on population size, on consumption per person, and on the technologies used, and all three vary greatly between regions.
Sustainability requires that renewable resources be used no faster than they are replenished and that waste be produced no faster than it can be absorbed.
Human population growth rate has been declining globally for decades, while total population continues to rise.
disqualifying_errors: Attributing resource pressure to population size alone, ignoring consumption and technology.
Claiming a renewable resource cannot be depleted.
Claiming global population is growing at an accelerating rate.
topics.out_of_scope: Demographic projection methodology and carrying capacity estimation are beyond this course.

relationships: Defending a design means stating the evidence, the assumptions, the uncertainty, and what result would change the recommendation.
Uncertainty is a reason to state the range of outcomes and to build in adaptability, not a reason to withhold a recommendation.
The strongest objection is addressed directly rather than omitted.
disqualifying_errors: Presenting a recommendation with no acknowledgement of its uncertainties.
Treating uncertainty as grounds for taking no position at all.
Omitting the strongest objection to the proposed design.
topics.out_of_scope: Decision theory under uncertainty and formal risk management frameworks are beyond this course.
